title: Adventure settings
titlePageNote: Every field except the title is optional and printed only when filled in.
field.title: Title
field.header: Header (a small line above the title)
field.subtitle: Subtitle
field.author: Author
field.extra: Extra row at the bottom (for example the playing characters)
easyRead: Easy-read copies in the player PDF
themeNote: Changing the theme changes only the look. The text, codex and maps are never touched.
app.updateWeekly: Check for a newer version once a week
app.updateNote: Scriptorum only reads one small file from the project's web address. It downloads an update only when you click Download and install, and never installs anything by itself.
app.updateAddressNote: Leave it empty to use the built-in address. Whatever the address, Scriptorum installs only updates signed with the project's key.
colours.cssSkipped: Shift was held at start, so the palette's own stylesheet is not used until the next start.
colours.name: Name of the new palette
colours.lowContrast: {count} text colours read at less than 4.5 contrast, such as {text} on {background} ({ratio}). You can still save the palette.
modules.note: Modules are installed once and used by every adventure. An adventure never carries its modules: send the adventure's .scav file and, for each module that did not come with Scriptorum, its .scmod file.
modules.name: Name
colours.unsaved: The new palette has colours that are not saved. Save them?
columnTooNarrow: Each column is only {mm} mm wide, which reads badly. Use fewer columns or smaller margins.
pageStartsNote: Which elements start a new page. A framed element never starts a page inside another frame.
compact: Compact: nothing starts a new page by itself
booklet.order.fold: Fold order: the sheets fold into a booklet
booklet.order.side-by-side: Side by side, in reading order
printNote: File ▸ Export makes the booklet and the print-shop version. The booklet has no links or bookmarks; the print-shop version has crop marks and is PDF/A.
languageNote: Used for the PDF, for spell check and for the words Scriptorum prints.
modules.reason.alwaysOn: Scriptorum falls back on this module, so it stays.
modules.reason.inUse: This one is in use. Choose another first.
modules.reason.bundled: It comes with Scriptorum, which would install it again at the next start. It can be disabled.
modules.reason.bundledSave: Every Scriptorum already has this module, so it needs no file.
modules.confirm.disable: Disable {name} {version}? It stays on this computer but is offered nowhere until you enable it again.
modules.confirm.usedBy: These adventures on your Recent files list use it and will open in protected mode: {adventures}. Other adventures may use it too.
modules.confirm.usedByNone: No adventure on your Recent files list uses it. Other adventures may use it; they will open in protected mode.
